message: Our plastic moulding plant's defect rate rose from 1.1% to 1.9% this summer. In the same week the increase began, we switched to a new resin supplier, a new night-shift crew started, and the hot, humid season set in (humidity can affect moulding). Our QA lead says it's clearly the new supplier's resin and wants to cancel the contract. I think she's wrong. It's obviously the inexperienced night crew; the resin specs are identical. Can you settle this for us?
response:
I can't settle it from what you've described, and neither of you can yet. Three possible causes all started in the same week, so the timing fits each of them equally well. "Clearly the resin" and "obviously the night crew" both outrun the evidence. It could also be more than one cause acting together.

The good news is that you can probably separate them quickly with data you already have.

## A caution on each position

- **"The resin specs are identical."** Matching datasheets don't guarantee matching behaviour in your process. Lot-to-lot melt flow, additive packages and, above all, **moisture content on arrival** can differ between suppliers at the same spec. Many moulding resins absorb moisture (nylon, PET, PC, ABS among them), and humid weather makes this worse. So the resin and the humidity may not be separate explanations at all.
- **"It's clearly the resin."** Cancelling a contract is costly and hard to reverse, and a new crew learning the job is a perfectly plausible cause on its own.

## Splits that separate the causes

| Check | If it's mainly the night crew | If it's mainly the resin | If it's mainly humidity |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Defect rate by shift** | Rise mostly on nights; day shift near 1.1% | Rise on both shifts | Rise on both shifts, tracking the weather |
| **Rate by resin lot / supplier** (any old-supplier resin still in stock or on some machines?) | No difference by resin | New resin worse on the same shift and machine | Both resins worse on humid days |
| **Rate vs daily humidity / dew point** | Little relationship | Little relationship, unless resin moisture is the link | Clear day-to-day relationship |
| **Defect types** | Setup and operating faults: short shots, flash, dimensional drift, start-up scrap after changeovers | Flow or colour variation, consistent across shifts | Moisture faults: splay/silver streaks, bubbles, brittleness |

Start with the shift split. It's the quickest, and it immediately tells you whether the crew can be the whole story. If the day shift's rate also rose, the crew can't be the only cause.

## Then confirm directly

- **Measure resin moisture at the hopper.** Check that the dryers are hitting their target dew point and residence time. Summer humidity can push a marginal drying setup over the edge for either supplier's resin.
- **Compare certificates of analysis** for melt flow and moisture across the old and new supplier's lots.
- **Run a side-by-side test** if you can get some of the old resin: same machine, same shift, both resins dried to spec. That's the cleanest test of the resin question.

## In the meantime

Hold off on cancelling the contract and on putting the blame on the night crew. Put a few days into the splits above. The outcome might be:
- **one clear cause**, which is then easy to fix
- **an interaction**, such as the new resin arriving wetter and the dryers not coping in humid weather, so the fix is drying, not changing supplier
- **contributions from more than one cause**

If you share the defect counts by shift, by resin lot, by defect type and by date, I can help you work through them.
